messages:
Maya Chen: Quick idea — propose a small, explicit 'adapter' stub interface that the control plane uses to talk to runtimes across hosted / dedicated / private. Goal: single compile-time contract, runtime-specific impls behind it so rollouts and fallbacks are predictable.

Maya Chen: Benefits: clear escape hatch for private ops, easier canary across environments, single place to handle KMS/telemetry mapping, and avoids ad-hoc config parsing.

Maya Chen: Rough sketch (conceptual):
```go
type Adapter interface {
  Serve(req *Request) (*Response, error)
  TranslateConfig(cfg map[string]string) error
  Health() HealthStatus
  ConfigureTenant(tenantID string, cfg TenantConfig) error
}
```

Zane Ortiz: +1 for an interface. Concern: perf overhead if we add abstraction layer per-request — can we inline or generate fast paths?

Leo Park: We can have Adapter implementations that expose a RawServe() optimized path. The interface above is conceptual; we can use codegen to emit thin callsites for hot paths.

Sara V: Another thing — telemetry & audit. Hosted needs token-level tracing; private may not allow export. Adapter should surface a 'TelemetryCapabilities' struct so control plane can decide enriched metrics vs local-only.

Ethan Li: Important to enumerate invariants: authN/O, KV cache semantics, fallback/model-variant behaviour, and serialization formats. We need contract language about which invariants must be preserved regardless of impl.

Maya Chen: Good call. Proposal: add an `Invariants() []string` and a capability bitmask (SupportsPrefetch, SupportsKVCaching, SupportsTenantIsolation, AllowsExternalTelemetry). That way control plane can make routing/rollback decisions.

Zane Ortiz: FYI we already have some bits in runtime-adapter branch. Might be worth aligning names to avoid repeated churn.

Sara V: Edge case — private deployments with network partition or strict egress rules: adapter must support a "degraded mode" signal so control plane doesn't assume full feature set. Expose `Status()` with enumerated modes (NORMAL, DEGRADED, ISOLATED).

ops-bot: (ci) build passed for branch runtime-adapter/shim-197.

Leo Park: Action items: 1) Draft RFC with API surface + capability matrix, 2) Prototype a minimal stub that wraps existing runtime, 3) Perf baseline for per-request overhead. Volunteers: Maya + Leo = RFC & stub, Zane = perf baseline, Sara = compliance/capabilities matrix.

Maya Chen: I'll open RFC today and attach the sketch + compatibility checklist. Ping me if you want to be on the review list. Also thinking we should include a short example of config translation for KMS and audit toggles to show expected behaviour in private vs hosted. :sparkles:

Zane Ortiz: SGTM. I'll start a perf harness that compares direct runtime calls vs adapter-wrapped calls (latency + p50/p99 + allocations).

Ethan Li: If RFC touches auth/invariants I'll add a section for tenancy and KV-cache semantics.

Sara V: I'll draft the capabilities matrix and map which features can be safely optional in private.

Maya Chen: cool — thanks all. Closing loop in the RFC thread.
